integrity.summary: Two unresolved matters: a party disciplinary referral to the EFCC and police, which he denies, and an unresolved question about his declared age. Neither is a legal finding.
integrity.analysis:
Two matters are on the public record, and neither is a legal finding. First, Vanguard reported on 3 November 2026 that the DLA's national chairman, Samuel Memeh, announced that the party's disciplinary committee, which had invited Adebisi to appear on 30 August 2026, had directed the suspension of all campaign activities associated with his candidacy. The dispute concerns a personal financial undertaking, including an allegedly dishonoured cheque, said to have been made before the 20 August substitution primary. The party said it had referred the matter to the EFCC and the Inspector-General of Police. In remarks relayed from a Punch interview, Adebisi rejected the suspension, said he remains the legitimate candidate, denied financial impropriety, said he had spent more than N90m reviving the party, described an N40m cheque to Memeh as an undated guarantee, and accused Memeh of trying to negotiate with another candidate. As of 28 November 2026, no EFCC or police statement confirming an investigation and no final committee decision were found.

Second, VeroRecord reported that UK Companies House filings for a director named Moses Olusoji Adebisi give an April 1994 birth month and year. That would not match the age of 35 on INEC's list. The report itself says the identity link is an inference, that Companies House does not verify filings, that the candidate's nomination form was not reviewed, and that no INEC or court finding exists. No asset declaration was found.
strengths: He has publicly responded to the party's allegations, giving his own account of the payments
limitations: Both matters rest on party statements, his own denials and an inference from company filings; none has been tested by an investigator or court
The underlying Punch reports could not be retrieved directly in this pass
unknowns: Whether the EFCC or police opened an investigation

experience.summary: No public-office experience. His background is in small private ventures and political organising, much of it self-described.
experience.analysis:
Adebisi has not held elected or appointed public office, so this category rests on his private and political-organising record, much of which is self-described. INEC's final list records only a First School Leaving Certificate, a Senior Secondary School Certificate and a BSc, and gives his age as 35. OurNigeria reports that he comes from Gbongan in Ayedaade LGA of Osun State, that he declared a BSc in Human Resource Management from ISCG University in Benin Republic, and that he co-founded Thrillers Travels, which launched in Lagos in September 2023 with a Canadian work-visa scheme. The same profile lists him as founder of the Thrillers Human Development Foundation and, in 2024, of the Nigerian Liberty Movement, an association that sought but did not obtain registration as a party.

VeroRecord's summary of UK Companies House filings shows a Moses Olusoji Adebisi as director of two small UK companies, incorporated in 2022 and 2024 and later dissolved after strike-off notices. The report treats the identity link as an inference. NAN described him in August 2026 as a U.S.-based businessman, and he told Arise he had returned from the United States to run. Claims of Harvard study, a fellowship and an honorary doctorate are his own and were not confirmed. None of these roles involved managing public budgets, legislation or a public workforce. He became the DLA candidate through a substitution primary in August 2026, replacing Samuel Memeh.
strengths: Has founded and run small private ventures and a political association
limitations: No public-office, legislative or large-organisation management record found
unknowns: Size, revenue and outcomes of the businesses and foundation he leads

foreign.summary: The only foreign-related statement found is a reported pledge of 'free visas' to Canada and the UK, which a Nigerian government could not grant on its own.
foreign.analysis: Arise's interview report says Adebisi would give people free visas to Canada and the UK. Visas for those countries are issued by their governments, so such a pledge could at most mean negotiated arrangements; the transcript is partly garbled and the exact commitment is unclear. No other foreign-policy positions were found.
